'''Guerschon Yabusele''' ({{IPA|fr|ɡɛʁʃɔn jabuzele}}; ''GAIR-shun YAH-boo-ZELL-ay;'' born December 17, 1995) is a French professional [[basketball]] player for [[Panathinaikos B.C.|Panathinaikos]] of the [[Greek Basketball League]] (GBL) and the [[EuroLeague]]. He primarily plays at the [[power forward (basketball)|power forward]] position. Yabusele represents the [[France men's national basketball team|French national team]] in international competitions, with whom he won silver medals at the [[Basketball at the 2020 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2020]] and [[Basketball at the 2024 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2024 Olympics]]. Yabusele was considered one of the best international prospects for the [[2016 NBA draft]].{{cite web|first=Sam|last=Vecenie|title=NBA Draft Prospect Rankings|url=http://www.cbssports.com/nba/draft/prospect-rankings|work=[[CBS Sports]]|access-date=March 9, 2016}}{{cite web|title=Guerschon Yabusele|url=http://www.draftexpress.com/profile/Guerschon-Yabusele-66311/|website=DraftExpress.com|access-date=March 9, 2016|archive-date=March 8, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210308040122/http://www.draftexpress.com/profile/Guerschon-Yabusele-66311/|url-status=dead}}{{cite web|title=Guerschon Yabusele|url=http://www.nbadraft.net/players/guerschon-yabusele|website=NBADraft.net|access-date=March 9, 2016}}{{cite web|title=A list of international players who might tempt the Sixers|url=http://www.philly.com/philly/blogs/pattisonave/A-list-of-international-players-who-might-tempt-the-Sixers.html|work=[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]]|date=February 5, 2016|access-date=March 9, 2016}} He was drafted with the 16th overall pick by the [[Boston Celtics]] and played for them from [[2017–18 Boston Celtics season|2017]] to [[2018–19 Boston Celtics season|2019]], splitting time with Boston's [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[Maine Celtics|Maine Red Claws]]. While in [[Boston]], Yabusele became a fan favorite despite playing few minutes and was nicknamed the "Dancing Bear."{{cite news|title=Guerschon Yabusele Reportedly Getting Waived Leads To Some Wild Twitter Reactions {{!}} Boston Celtics {{!}} NESN.com|url=https://nesn.com/2019/07/guerschon-yabusele-reportedly-getting-waived-leads-to-some-wild-twitter-reactions/|date=July 10, 2019|access-date=January 11, 2020}} Yabusele has also played in the [[Chinese Basketball Association]] and the lower-level French [[LNB Pro B]]. He signed with [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]] in [[2021–22 Real Madrid Baloncesto season|2021]], and won a [[EuroLeague]] title in [[2023 EuroLeague championship game|2023]]. After an impressive performance for France during the 2024 Olympics, he returned to the NBA and signed with the [[Philadelphia 76ers]]. Yabusele has also played for the [[New York Knicks]] and the [[Chicago Bulls]]. ==Early life== Yabusele was born and raised in [[Dreux|Dreux, France]], to parents who emigrated from [[The Democratic Republic of Congo]].{{cite web|first=Kevin|last=Wang|title=Meet Guerschon Yabusele, the Celtics' big, French 'dancing bear'|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/18850442/boston-celtics-guerschon-yabusele-ready-nba-year-china|website=ESPN.com|date=March 8, 2017|access-date=October 18, 2018}} In his youth, Yabusele trained as a boxer.{{cite web|title=Phoenix Suns Pre-Draft Workouts Day 9: A Diamond in the Rough?|url=http://www.brightsideofthesun.com/2016/6/3/11852930/phoenix-suns-pre-draft-workouts-day-8-a-diamond-in-the-rough|website=BrightSideOfTheSun.com|date=June 3, 2016|access-date=August 29, 2024}} He began playing basketball with the youth sections of [[Chorale Roanne Basket]] in 2012, competing with their under-21 team. ==Professional career== ===Chorale Roanne (2013–2015)=== Yabusele joined the Chorale Roanne team in the [[LNB Pro B]] in 2013 and finished the season averaging 1.5 points per game in 8 appearances. The next season, he averaged six points, four rebounds, and 1.7 assists.{{cite web|title=Guerschon Yabusele|url=http://basketball.eurobasket.com/player/Guerschon_Yabusele/France/SPO_Rouen_Basket/263342|website=Eurobasket.com|access-date=March 9, 2016}} ===Rouen Métropole (2015–2016)=== Yabusele signed with [[Rouen Métropole Basket]] of the [[LNB Pro A]], the top league in France, in the summer of 2015. He made the decision to help his NBA draft stock.{{cite web|first=Alexandre|last=Lacoste|title=Guerschon Yabusele Trois Ans À Rouen|url=http://www.bebasket.fr/a/51887-guerschon-yabusele-trois-ans-a-rouen|website=BeBasket.fr|access-date=March 9, 2016|language=fr|archive-date=July 7, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150707003253/http://www.bebasket.fr/a/51887-guerschon-yabusele-trois-ans-a-rouen|url-status=dead}} Yabusele wound up being one of 13 international underclassmen, and one of four Frenchmen, to officially enter their names for the [[2016 NBA draft]]. He was projected to be either a late first round or early second round selection but surprised many by going 16th overall in the draft to Boston.{{cite web|title=DraftExpress - Guerschon Yabusele On July 8, 2026, Yabusele signed a three-year contract with [[Panathinaikos B.C.|Panathinaikos]] of the [[Greek Basketball League]] (GBL) and the [[EuroLeague]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/en/euroleague/news/panathinaikos-brings-guerschon-yabusele-back-to-the-euroleague/|title=Panathinaikos brings Guerschon Yabusele back to the EuroLeague|date=July 8, 2026|website=euroleaguebasketball.net|access-date=July 8, 2026}} ==National team career== ===Junior team=== Yabusele played for the France under-18 team at the [[2013 FIBA Europe Under-18 Championship]] and later with the under-20 team at the [[2014 FIBA Europe Under-20 Championship]] and the [[2015 FIBA Europe Under-20 Championship]]. ===Senior team=== He played with Les Bleus at the [[Basketball at the 2020 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2020 Olympics]], where he won a silver medal, as well as at [[EuroBasket 2022]], once again winning silver. He also played at the [[2023 FIBA Basketball World Cup|2023 World Cup]].{{cite web|title=Guerschon YABUSELE at the FIBA Basketball World Cup 2023|url=https://www.fiba.basketball/it/basketballworldcup/2023/player/Guerschon-Yabusele|website=FIBA.basketball|access-date=August 8, 2024|language=it}} He played a key role in France's campaign at [[Basketball at the 2024 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2024 Olympics]]. Despite having a minor role in the preliminary round, he led the team to a quarter-final victory over [[Canada men's national basketball team|Canada]] with 22 points and 5 rebounds.{{cite web|title="Dancing Bear" Yabusele is France's "Knockout King"|url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/events/mens-olympic-basketball-tournament-paris-2024/news/dancing-bear-yabusele-is-frances-knockout-king|website=FIBA.basketball|date=August 8, 2024|access-date=August 8, 2024}} He then scored 17 points on 7-for-11 shooting, as well as 7 rebounds, to lead France to a semi-final win over [[Germany men's national basketball team|Germany]], to qualify for their second straight Olympic final.{{cite web|title=France defense bottles up Schroder and Franz|url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/events/mens-olympic-basketball-tournament-paris-2024/news/france-defense-bottles-up-schroder-and-franz|website=FIBA.basketball|date=August 8, 2024|access-date=August 8, 2024}} In the final against the [[United States men's national basketball team|United States]], Yabusele scored 20 points, including a baseline [[Posterized|poster dunk]] on [[LeBron James]], before eventually losing and finishing with a silver medal.{{cite web|title=It's Steph's world: Curry's hot shooting gets USA another gold|url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/events/mens-olympic-basketball-tournament-paris-2024/news/its-stephs-world-currys-hot-shooting-gets-usa-another-gold|website=FIBA.basketball|date=August 10, 2024|access-date=August 11, 2024}} After the tournament, he was named to the tournament's [[FIBA Men's Olympics All-Star Five|All-Second Team]].{{cite web|title=Gilgeous-Alexander, Bogdanovic, F. Wagner, Yabusele, Antetokounmpo named to Paris 2024 All-Second Team|url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/events/mens-olympic-basketball-tournament-paris-2024/news/gilgeous-alexander-bogdanovic-f-wagner-yabusele-antetokounmpo-named-to-paris|website=FIBA.basketball|date=August 10, 2024|access-date=August 11, 2024}} Yabusele led France at [[EuroBasket 2025]]. On September 2, he scored a career-high 36 points to lead France to a 83–76 win over [[Poland men's national basketball team|Poland]] in the group phase.{{Cite web |date=2025-09-02 |title=France end Polish win streak behind Yabusele’s career high |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/events/fiba-eurobasket-2025/news/france-end-polish-win-streak-behind-yabuseles-career-high |access-date=2025-09-03
